The letter to the Gazette addresses inaccuracies and a lack of context in their April 5th, 2025 article concerning ACPS budget and administrative staffing.

It explains that the reported 54% increase in administrative roles is based on a broad internal classification system that includes school-based leaders, curriculum directors, and support staff, not solely departmental administrators. Many of these roles were reclassifications of existing positions that are not new positions, and they were reclassified following a compensation study to remain regionally competitive.

The letter outlines that staffing changes have been made carefully and strategically to meet the growing needs in special education, student mental health and safety, technology, and capital projects. These roles support enrollment growth, students with special needs, the launch of new programs, and the opening of new school facilities. Importantly, the letter also emphasizes that continued administrative growth is both necessary and expected. As the division opens new schools and implements new programs, we will continue to need school-based and central leadership to ensure

strong implementation, student support, and accountability. This growth reflects the community's priorities for expanding capacity rather than overcrowding existing facilities. Some key points from the letter. The 54% increase in administrative roles cited in the article is based on an internal pay grade grouping, not on newly created central positions. Many of these roles were existing positions reclassified due to added responsibilities or compensation adjustments from a 2022 market study, competitive market study.

The administrator category includes a range of staff: school leaders, counseling directors, special education coordinators, athletic directors, project managers. Administrative staff and growth has been strategic and student focused in terms of managing capital projects, expanding special education services, increasing school safety and mental health support, meeting technology demands, launching new programs and sites.

This article was published without consulting ACPS, missing the opportunity to clarify these points with readers. ACPS remains committed to transparency, responsible budgeting, and clear communication with the community.
